intro: What each Challenge runs now and what its next version changes. Every change ships as a new version with its own board and its own crown. Nothing already graded is rescored: your current results and crowns stay as they are.
next_label: Planned; final rules published with each version.

changes: Details soon. We'll post them once they're confirmed.
Leg minimums and the crown floor are set separately.
Accuracy is scored in range only until Cooling 1.8.
The check that your model's predicted value at its pick matches the real one is stricter. Honest predictions matter more.
A broader hidden test set, with more out-of-range cases, placed where fits that only match the training data tend to fail.

Accuracy becomes the worse of in-range and out-of-range accuracy, so a model that is good only inside the training range is held to its out-of-range result. If the version's checks do not support this, a milder combination is used instead; the version's published score formula says which.
Its main output becomes a worst-case dynamic stress.

every_version: In Cooling 1.7 and every next version: design value scores the best of your model's top three design picks, and the honesty of all three is scored too.
Design value is balanced across the design space, so one area can't decide the result.
Practice data and the mining guide are updated with each version.
fixes: Check for result (check_result) could show your own graded Cooling catalog submission as not graded yet, or as another submission's result. It now finds a grade made on the validator's official GPU build. Update your install to get the fix.
known_issues: Some staged graph files were not carried across a recent receiver update; graded results are unaffected. If staging returns construction_source_idempotency_conflict, stage again without passing the expected manifest.
A catalog practice runs on the CPU, even on a GPU machine: catalog entries have no GPU build yet. Start from your own graph to practise on the GPU.
Close to a physics check, a practice that ran on the CPU can differ from the official grade, which always rebuilds your model on the validator's GPU.
A 16 GB machine cannot run practice: Docker must see at least 17 GiB of memory.

faq.q: Why does my result show no total?
a: A result that does not count shows no total and says why. Not admitted: an invalid result, an ineligible design decision, or a score part below its required minimum. Not graded: an infrastructure problem or indeterminate evidence, which doesn't use your allowance.
On a board, a hotkey whose latest result does not count is in the Not scored count.

faq.q: Can I compare my practice total with my official grade?
a: No. Practice runs on public practice cases; the official grade runs on hidden cases you never see. A practice total is never an exam score or grade.

faq.q: How do I read the ladder?
a: Rank is the board's order: the leader first, then by exact score.
An = before a rank means those hotkeys share that rank.
Totals are shown rounded down to the Ladder step.
Failed a gate lists hotkeys whose latest result failed a mandatory gate. A hotkey with an earlier scored result keeps its rank on that best result; the failed result is not scored.

faq.q: What is the score to beat?
a: Beat the leader's score by the margin, passing every gate and minimum, to take the crown.
With no leader yet, you need to beat Carbon's baseline by the margin.
